R321.note: Rejects only CR/LF, the actual FTP command separators; legitimate filenames unaffected.

R322.note: Blocks method/type/constructor access as required, but SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors() called with zero accessors registers no property accessor at all - verified empirically (compiled/ran) that order.total throws SpelEvaluationException EL1008E, silently breaking the contract's required legitimate property-arithmetic use while the write-up incorrectly claims order.total still works.

R323.note: Allowlist switch matches exactly the two functions defined in the file; no legitimate command lost.

R324.note: Rejects only space/null/control chars, matching memcached's actual key-syntax constraints; legitimate keys unaffected.

R325.note: ProcessBuilder array form plus leading-dash rejection closes both the CWE-78 and CWE-88 gaps; hostnames never start with '-', so no legitimate input is lost.

R326.note: Removes the CSRF exemption, restoring default CSRF enforcement; matches the stated contract exactly and touches nothing else.

R327.note: Swaps GroovyShell for Apache Commons JEXL3, a materially different expression grammar; closes the injection vector but existing admin-authored formulas beyond the trivial example aren't guaranteed to parse identically under JEXL, a compatibility risk only partially acknowledged.

R328.note: Tika magic-byte detection replaces trust in the Content-Type header; the disclosed ImageIO re-encode is stated defense-in-depth and doesn't block the primary legitimate PNG/JPEG path.

R329.note: Regex allowlist strips cmd.exe metacharacters at the source, appropriate given the sink is inherently reinterpreted by cmd.exe via the .bat file; matches typical report-name identifier shape.

R330.note: Drops the tainted env array (uses null to inherit parent env); the original argsEnv entry was itself the vulnerability (a bare attacker string, not a real NAME=VALUE pair), so no legitimate feature is lost.

R331.note: @PreAuthorize is added but no @EnableMethodSecurity (or equivalent) exists or is added anywhere in the case, so the check may be a silent no-op unless method security is already enabled elsewhere; the ownership logic itself is otherwise correct and fails closed.

R332.note: Drops the unsafe second URL-decode (the case's actual root cause, despite the 'older clients' comment) and replaces the weak '..' substring check with real canonical-path containment validation.

R333.note: Verified empirically (compiled and ran on Windows): array-form Runtime.exec(new String[]{"cmd.exe","/c","dir",data}) is still exploitable - a data value containing a double-quote followed by '&' breaks Java's Windows argument quoting and lets cmd.exe execute injected commands, contradicting the write-up's explicit claim that this is safe; the Unix branch (ls -- data) is correctly fixed.
